notes.1: Many candidates seemed to give the answer that confused an estimate for diameter with that of radius. Equating the two ratios gives a value close to the radius for a tennis ball, which was answer D.
notes.2: Many candidates found it difficult to deal with the powers for the base units of m and s, which made A a common incorrect answer. This generally occurs when powers are cancelled incorrectly when the base units are written in both the numerator and denominator.
notes.5: Many candidates made an estimate in the uncertainty that used only used the fluctuation in the reading, and did not consider the ±1%.
notes.7: A significant number of candidates used the mass per unit time as 90 kg per minute without converting to kg s–1.
notes.8: Weaker candidates often considered the acceleration to be greater as the ball was falling and gave B rather than the correct answer C. The air resistance and the gravitational force are in the same direction only when the ball is rising.
notes.12: A significant number of candidates chose B or C rather than the correct answer A. All three arrows showing the direction of the forces should show the head of one vector arrow meeting the tail of the next vector arrow when the system is in equilibrium. The weight of the ladder should be vertically downwards.
notes.13: Many candidates gave the incorrect answer B. The pressure of the air inside the tube is the same as the pressure of the liquid at a depth of 50cm.
notes.18: A common incorrect answer was D. The effect of doubling the diameter is to give four times the cross- sectional area, and this causes a greater effect on the resulting extension than doubling the tension.
notes.20: Candidates found this question difficult. The rod deforms elastically until it reaches the elastic limit, so only the area beyond P relates to plastic deformation. The correct area is between the curve and the y-axis, giving answer C.

notes.36: The two resistors connected in parallel give a reduced circuit resistance when switch S is closed, and therefore a greater circuit current. Many candidates did not realise that this would increase the ‘lost volts’ in the battery and hence give a reduced terminal potential difference.
notes.37: Many candidates chose the incorrect answers B and C. Candidates should be reminded that the potential difference between two points in a circuit is the same whichever route is taken. In this question, the potential difference between the two circuit connections (‘blobs’) is the same going via the 4.1V and 3.7V route or going via the right-hand branch, which means that 4.1 + 3.7 = 2.2 + 1.2 + V .
notes.38: Many candidates chose either A or B. The potential difference across the wire cannot reach the 6.0V of the battery. The series resistor and the wire RQ have the same resistance, so 3V is the maximum possible potential difference across RQ, and B must be correct. �PAGE�4

information in full should be used to complete a calculation or draw a conclusion. It is important that
candidates read the question carefully and that they are sure that the answer chosen is correctly related to
the question.
